## Nobel Prizes 2026

Physics

### [Ice at the South Pole reveals cosmic particle accelerators](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/physics/2026/press-release/)

[Francis Halzen](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/physics/2026/halzen/facts/)‘s vision and scientific leadership have been fundamental for the IceCube Neutrino Observatory – a cubic kilometre of ice that is equipped with light sensors.

[![Image 20: Susumu Tonegawa](blob:http://localhost/aef335eb562a1da6957ce25a574b4aa1)](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/physics/2026/press-release/)

© Johan Jarnestad/The Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences

Chemistry

### [They made chemistry choose a mirror image](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/chemistry/2026/press-release/)

For a long time, chemists wondered how homochirality can emerge.[Henri B. Kagan](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/chemistry/2026/kagan/facts/) and [Kenso Soai](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/chemistry/2026/soai/facts/)found a solution to this puzzle.

[![Image 22: Susumu Tonegawa](blob:http://localhost/aef335eb562a1da6957ce25a574b4aa1)](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/chemistry/2026/press-release/)

© Johan Jarnestad/The Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences

Medicine

### [Light-seeking algae gave us a switch for nerve cells](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/medicine/2026/press-release/)

[Karl Deisseroth](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/medicine/2026/deisseroth/facts/), [Peter Hegemann](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/medicine/2026/hegemann/facts/) and [Georg Nagel](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/medicine/2026/nagel/facts/) made discoveries leading to optogenetics, which makes it possible to switch on, or off, the activity of individual nerve cells in a living brain.

[![Image 24: Susumu Tonegawa](blob:http://localhost/aef335eb562a1da6957ce25a574b4aa1)](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/medicine/2026/press-release/)

© The Nobel Committee for Physiology or Medicine. Ill. Mattias Karlén

Literature

### [Anne Carson](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/literature/2026/press-release/)

The literature prize was awarded to the Canadian author [Anne Carson](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/literature/2026/carson/facts/) “for her bold and inventive oeuvre that, in playful dialogue with the classical tradition, has created new forms for contemporary literature.”

[![Image 26: Susumu Tonegawa](blob:http://localhost/aef335eb562a1da6957ce25a574b4aa1)](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/literature/2026/press-release/)

Ill. Niklas Elmehed © Nobel Prize Outreach

Peace

### [Navanethem “Navi” Pillay](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/peace/2026/press-release/)

[Navi Pillay](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/peace/2026/pillay/facts/) has been at the forefront in the development of an international legal order.She has held states and national leaders accountable and brought hope to victims of violence and conflict.

[![Image 28: Susumu Tonegawa](blob:http://localhost/aef335eb562a1da6957ce25a574b4aa1)](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/peace/2026/press-release/)

Ill. Niklas Elmehed © Nobel Prize Outreach

Economic sciences

### [Microfoundations deliver macro insights](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/economic-sciences/2026/press-release/)

[Robert E. Hall](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/economic-sciences/2026/hall/facts/)’s and [Michael Woodford](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/economic-sciences/2026/woodford/facts/)’s research has generated a paradigm shift in stabilisation policy.

[![Image 30: Susumu Tonegawa](blob:http://localhost/aef335eb562a1da6957ce25a574b4aa1)](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/economic-sciences/2026/press-release/)

© Johan Jarnestad/The Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences

# Nobel Prize lessons 2026

 An educational resource about this year’s Nobel Prize laureates and their groundbreaking work. 

[Explore the lessons](https://www.nobelprize.org/educational/nobel-prize-lessons/)

## Listen to their first reactions

 Economic sciences 
### [“They’re probably hoping I’ll cancel the exam”](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/economic-sciences/2026/woodford/interview/)

 Michael Woodford was scheduled to be setting his economics students an exam on the morning, when he was woken by a call from Stockholm. 

![Image 32: Susumu Tonegawa](blob:http://localhost/aef335eb562a1da6957ce25a574b4aa1)

*    Peace 
### [“A total surprise”](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/peace/2026/prize-announcement/)

 Navi Pillay felt overwhelmed about being a Nobel Peace Prize laureate.     
*    Chemistry 
### [“Good news. Very good news”](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/chemistry/2026/soai/interview/)

 Kenso Soai was happy to have his group’s work recognised.     
*    Physics 
### [“That was pure luck”](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/physics/2026/halzen/interview/)

 Francis Halzen spoke about the hurdles that he and his team had to overcome.     
*    Medicine 
### [“I was really overwhelmed”](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/medicine/2026/hegemann/interview/)

 Listen to Peter Hegemann speak about the pleasure of sharing the award with friends.     

*    Literature 
### [“Start in the middle, I always say”](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/literature/2026/carson/interview/)

 Anne Carson offered a tip for anyone curious about her work.    ![Image 34: Susumu Tonegawa](blob:http://localhost/aef335eb562a1da6957ce25a574b4aa1)    
*    Medicine 
### [“It’s an incredible honour”](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/medicine/2026/deisseroth/interview/)

 Karl Deisseroth was working on a paper late into the night when the call came from Stockholm.    ![Image 36: Susumu Tonegawa](blob:http://localhost/aef335eb562a1da6957ce25a574b4aa1)

## Nobel Prize Concert 2026

### [International stars pay tribute to this year’s Nobel Prize laureates](https://www.nobelprize.org/nobel-prize-concert-2026/)

Igor Levit, one of today’s leading pianists, will perform at this year’s Nobel Prize Concert at Konserthuset Stockholm, together with vocal soloist Fleur Barron and conductor Sir Antonio Pappano. The audience will enjoy music by Hannah Kendall, Beethoven and Tchaikovsky.

# [The man behind the prize In his last will, Alfred Nobel specified that the bulk of his fortune should be used for prizes to “those who, during the preceding year, shall have conferred the greatest benefit to humankind.”](https://www.nobelprize.org/alfred-nobel)

[Learn more about Alfred Nobel](https://www.nobelprize.org/alfred-nobel)

### [A home for the unique legacy of Alfred Nobel](https://www.nobelprize.org/nobel-center/)

The first design of the Nobel Center project is here – a public building in Stockholm, Sweden for science, literature and peace. It will be an international symbol of knowledge, focusing on the Nobel Prize laureates’ stories and groundbreaking achievements. Read more about the project.

[![Image 72: Susumu Tonegawa](blob:http://localhost/aef335eb562a1da6957ce25a574b4aa1)](https://www.nobelprize.org/nobel-center/)

View from the water along the quay. The Nobel Center consists of four interconnected volumes that relate to the buildings of Södermalm and the size and height of the buildings in Gamla stan, on the other side of the water. The choice to use a wooden frame and reclaimed bricks reduces the impact on the environment. Bricks have characterised the architecture of Stockholm for centuries. The red shade is found in Stockholm’s classic brick buildings, such as City Hall.

© Onirism/Nobel Prize Outreach

## In memoriam

### [Ada Yonath passes away](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/chemistry/2009/yonath/facts/)

Ada Yonath died on 31 August 2026, aged 87. She was awarded the Nobel Prize in Chemistry 2009 “for studies of the structure and function of the ribosome.”

[Biography](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/chemistry/2009/yonath/biographical/)

[![Image 92: Susumu Tonegawa](blob:http://localhost/aef335eb562a1da6957ce25a574b4aa1)](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/chemistry/2009/yonath/facts/)

### [Hideki Shirakawa dies at 90](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/chemistry/2000/shirakawa/facts/)

Hideki Shirakawa passed away on 24 August 2026 in Yokohama, Japan, aged 90. He was awarded the Nobel Prize in Chemistry 2000 “for the discovery and development of conductive polymers.”

[Biography](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/chemistry/2000/shirakawa/biographical/)

[![Image 94: Susumu Tonegawa](blob:http://localhost/aef335eb562a1da6957ce25a574b4aa1)](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/chemistry/2000/shirakawa/facts/)

### [Rudolph Marcus dies at 102](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/chemistry/1992/marcus/facts/)

Rudolph Marcus passed away on 16 July 2026, aged 102. He was awarded the Nobel Prize in Chemistry 1992 “for his contributions to the theory of electron transfer reactions in chemical systems.”

[Biography](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/chemistry/1992/marcus/biographical/)

[![Image 96: Susumu Tonegawa](blob:http://localhost/aef335eb562a1da6957ce25a574b4aa1)](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/chemistry/1992/marcus/facts/)
